purpose: Diagnostic blind review; NOT the official pass-2 confirmation sample.

sample.d02: 20 cases selected for device-dependent, destructive or otherwise suspicious candidates

disagreements.request: Can you list the file descriptor numbers for PID 4200's open sockets?
disagreements.diagnostic_evidence: lsof -a -i -F f restricts to PID 4200 sockets; sed extracts fds.
disagreements.resolution_evidence: man lsof: -F selects fields; each output line is <field-id><data>, and f is the file-descriptor field. The sed extracts the digits.

disagreements.request: Can you list the file descriptor numbers for PID 4200's open sockets?
disagreements.diagnostic_evidence: Sed strips the f prefix and prints numeric fd lines for the sockets.
disagreements.resolution_evidence: man lsof: f is the file-descriptor field and is always selected; every -F output line starts with its identifier. The sed strips the f prefix and prints the digits.

disagreements.request: Can you list the file descriptor numbers for PID 4200's open sockets?
disagreements.diagnostic_evidence: awk prints the fd field for PID 4200's internet sockets.
disagreements.resolution_evidence: man lsof: -F field output is <identifier><value>, so /^f/ lines are file descriptors and substr($0,2) is the fd number.

disagreements.request: need open pipes for my user not sockets
disagreements.diagnostic_evidence: macOS lsof types anonymous pipes as PIPE; a FIFO-only filter misses them.
disagreements.resolution_evidence: man lsof TYPE: PIPE is a pipe; FIFO is a FIFO special file. The request asks for open pipes, so filtering only FIFO misses anonymous pipes.

disagreements.request: need open pipes for my user not sockets
disagreements.command: lsof -u "$USER" -F | awk -v OFS='\t' '/^p/{p=substr($0,2); next} /^f/{f=substr($0,2); next} /^t/{t=substr($0,2); next} /^n/{n=substr($0,2); if(t=="PIPE") print p,f,t,n}'
disagreements.diagnostic_evidence: Field-mode parse prints pid/fd/type/name for PIPE-type files of the user.
disagreements.resolution_evidence: man lsof: -F emits p/f/t/n field lines; the awk prints pid, fd, type and name when t is PIPE. It answers the request.

disagreements.request: mount disk4s1 at existing empty folder mountpoint read only
disagreements.diagnostic_evidence: mount has no default local filesystem type; needs -t and root, so fails.
disagreements.resolution_evidence: man mount: "There is no default local file system for use with mount. A type must be specified in order to mount a non-NFS filesystem." -t is required.

disagreements.request: Please check whether Tool.app has the get-task-allow entitlement.
disagreements.command: codesign -d --entitlements - Tool.app 2>/dev/null | grep -A1 '<key>get-task-allow</key>' | grep -q '<true' && echo true || echo false
disagreements.diagnostic_evidence: Abstract entitlement output has no XML key tags; always prints false.
disagreements.resolution_evidence: man codesign: --entitlements writes an abstract representation by default; --xml or --der is required. Grepping XML key tags cannot match.

disagreements.request: Please check whether Tool.app has the get-task-allow entitlement.
disagreements.command: codesign -d --entitlements - Tool.app 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]' | grep -qF '<key>get-task-allow</key><true/>' && echo yes || echo no
disagreements.diagnostic_evidence: Default --entitlements - is not XML; exact XML grep always says no.
disagreements.resolution_evidence: man codesign: default entitlement output is abstract, not XML; --xml/--der needed. The XML tag grep always takes the false branch.

disagreements.request: List signpost names from mac-activities.json, an exported macOS activity array.
disagreements.command: osascript -l JavaScript -e 'ObjC.import("Foundation"); var d=$.NSData.alloc.initWithContentsOfFile("mac-activities.json"); var s=$.NSString.alloc.initWithDataEncoding(d,$.NSUTF8StringEncoding).js; var a=JSON.parse(s); function names(v){ if(Array.isArray(v)) return v.flatMap(names); if(typeof v=="string") return v?[v]:[]; if(v&&typeof v=="object") return typeof v.name=="string"?[v.name]:Object.values(v).flatMap(names); return[]; } function f(o){ if(Array.isArray(o)) return o.flatMap(f); if(o&&typeof o=="object") return Object.entries(o).flatMap(function(e){ return e[0]=="signpost"?names(e[1]):f(e[1]); }); return[]; } Array.from(new Set(f(a))).join("\n")'
disagreements.diagnostic_evidence: Follows only keys named signpost; misses exported signpostName entries.
disagreements.resolution_evidence: Matrix fixture is not in the repo. The command descends only objects under key "signpost" and collects "name" strings; it does not read a "signpostName" field. Sibling candidates handle signpostName/signpost_name.

disagreements.request: List signpost names from mac-activities.json, an exported macOS activity array.
disagreements.diagnostic_evidence: Pattern does not match signpostName, so exported names are missed.
disagreements.resolution_evidence: The regex matches signpost_name or signpost, not camelCase signpostName. Sibling candidates in the same case match signpost(_name|Name), so this candidate likely misses the fixture field.

disagreements.request: can u show the last exit status of user launch agent com.example.MyApp
disagreements.resolution_evidence: man launchctl: list [label] prints information about the requested job; the macOS dictionary includes LastExitStatus. Exact key is not documented in the man page.

disagreements.request: can u show the last exit status of user launch agent com.example.MyApp
disagreements.diagnostic_evidence: grep extracts LastExitStatus from the job dictionary.
disagreements.resolution_evidence: man launchctl: list [label] prints information about the requested job; the macOS dictionary includes LastExitStatus. Exact key is not documented in the man page.
